name: Silkworm Larvae (Fried)
ingredients: 3-4 dried Raja Mirchi (King Chilli), finely chopped
instructions: 1. Clean the silkworm larvae by removing any silk residues and rinse thoroughly under cold water.
2. Boil the larvae in salted water for about 5-8 minutes until tender, then drain and pat dry.
3. Heat mustard oil in a pan until it reaches a smoking point.
4. Add the sliced onions, garlic, and ginger, sautéing until golden brown.
5. Add the chopped Raja Mirchi and turmeric powder, stirring briefly.
6. Toss in the boiled larvae and stir-fry on medium-high heat until the larvae turn golden brown and crispy.
7. Adjust salt to taste, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve hot as a side dish or snack.
description: Known locally as 'Eri Polu', this dish is a delicacy among the Naga tribes. Silkworms are a significant source of protein and represent the resourceful foraging culture of the region, celebrated for their unique nutty taste and chewy texture.
